comment: Source-first 65-atom coverage review after completing the ML formula, nondegeneracy, program-class, parity, theorem-range, and real-weight LAP routes. Every atom is directly or collectively covered; remaining source findings are ordinary formalization notes.

definition_borderline_set.reason: The finite union definition is exposed directly.
definition_borderline_set.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:363-367. V_C(X)=⋃_{x′} C(X)\C(X∪{x′}) is the set of admits that some insertion can displace.

definition_choice_distance.reason: The definition wrapper and displayed-formula theorem preserve both set-difference summands.
definition_choice_distance.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:212-217. For X₁⊆X₂, choice distance is |(X₁∩C(X₂))\C(X₁)|+|C(X₁)\C(X₂)|.

definition_choice_function_model.reason: The carrier and feasibility convention jointly expose the finite choice-function model.
definition_choice_function_model.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:171-180. A finite choice function maps every finite applicant pool X to a feasible chosen subset C(X)⊆X.

definition_choice_label_formula.reason: The binary label is defined and proved equal to one exactly on C(X).
definition_choice_label_formula.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:178-180. For applicant x_i in pool X, the binary label is y_i=C(X)_i=1 exactly when x_i∈C(X), and is 0 otherwise.

definition_consistency.reason: The Lean predicate preserves both containments and the equality conclusion.
definition_consistency.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:29-32. C is consistent when C(X₂)⊆X₁⊆X₂ implies C(X₂)=C(X₁).

definition_d_instability.reason: The Lean predicate has the same universal single-insertion bound.
definition_d_instability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:221-224. C is d-unstable when every one-applicant insertion changes at most d existing decisions under choice distance.

definition_fixed_threshold_score_formula.reason: The predictor and membership theorem expose the exact pool-independent threshold formula.
definition_fixed_threshold_score_formula.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:161-169. The fixed-threshold score classifier is f(x)=1{s(x)≥t}, with s:X→[0,1] and a pool-independent threshold t.

definition_general_variability.reason: The at-most and exact predicates encode the maximum of insertion and removal variability.
definition_general_variability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:375-379. General variability is max{max_X |V_C(X)|, max_X |A_C(X)|}.

definition_independence.reason: The applicant-wise always-or-never behavior is represented exactly.
definition_independence.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:208-216. C is independent when each applicant is either always chosen whenever available or never chosen whenever available.

definition_lap_assignment_choice.reason: Assignment incidence and the induced chosen-applicant rule are exposed directly.
definition_lap_assignment_choice.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:621-626. The assignment's incident applicants form C(X), and x_s denotes the applicant assigned to slot s.

definition_lap_model_objective.reason: The finite matching constraints and maximum-sum objective are formalized over real weights.
definition_lap_model_objective.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:610-621. A linear assignment problem chooses a maximum-real-weight applicant-slot matching with at most one edge incident to each applicant and slot.

definition_lap_slot_order.reason: The strict slot preference is exactly the real-weight comparison.
definition_lap_slot_order.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:618-620. Each slot's real weights, assumed tie-free, induce a strict total order over applicants.

definition_lap_slot_order_equivalence.reason: Slot-order equality is extensional and its quotient gives the canonical distinct-order count.
definition_lap_slot_order_equivalence.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:618-620. Two slots are equivalent exactly when they induce the same strict total order over all applicants.

definition_main_variability.reason: The borderline set plus at-most and exact predicates jointly expose the displayed maximum.
definition_main_variability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:234-242. For a q-acceptant 1-unstable rule, variability is max_X |⋃_{x′} C(X)\C(X∪{x′})|.

definition_ml_representation.reason: The representation predicate quantifies every pool and every offered applicant.
definition_ml_representation.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:247-250. An ML model represents C when one predictor f gives f(x_i)=C(X)_i for every applicant pool X and every x_i∈X.

definition_monotonicity.reason: The Lean predicate is the same containment implication.
definition_monotonicity.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:21-24. C is monotonic when X₁⊆X₂ implies C(X₁)⊆C(X₂).

definition_q_acceptance.reason: The paper-facing predicate has the same capacity equation and quantification.
definition_q_acceptance.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:185-188; cited publication:15-18. A choice function is q-acceptant when |C(X)|=min{q,|X|} for every finite input set X.

definition_q_representativeness.reason: The predicate exposes one global strict order and top-q choice.
definition_q_representativeness.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:37-44. C is q-representative when it is q-acceptant and one strict total order selects its top q applicants from every pool.

definition_queue_top_q.reason: The q-representative predicate exposes the same one-order top-q semantics.
definition_queue_top_q.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:196-200. A queue sorts applicants by one strict total order and chooses the top q elements of every input pool.

definition_rank_threshold_formula.reason: The top-q score predictor is proved equivalent on every pool to a pool-specific real threshold.
definition_rank_threshold_formula.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:252-258. The cohort-dependent rank model is f(x;X)=1{s(x)≥t_q(X)}, where t_q(X) is the q-th score in X.

definition_sequential_composition.reason: The list recursion implements the same remaining-pool construction.
definition_sequential_composition.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:306-310; cited publication:492-495. Sequential composition runs each choice rule on applicants remaining after earlier stages and unions all stage choices.

definition_substitutability.reason: The paper-facing predicate is the same nested-set implication.
definition_substitutability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:272-275; cited publication:17-19. C is substitutable when X₁⊆X₂ implies X₁∩C(X₂)⊆C(X₁).

definition_tight_d_instability.reason: The least-bound predicate is represented exactly; the later printed dk typo is separately noted.
definition_tight_d_instability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:221-224. C is tightly d-unstable when it is d-unstable but not (d-1)-unstable.

definition_total_order.reason: Lean uses the coherent distinct-pair reading; the printed unrestricted comparability wording is recorded as a note-only source correction.
definition_total_order.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:192-194. A strict total order is asymmetric and transitive, and compares every distinct pair of applicants.

definition_waitlisted_set.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:369-373. A_C(X)=⋃_{x*∈X} C(X\{x*})\C(X) is the set of applicants admitted after some removal.

definition_zero_instability.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:191-194. C is 0-unstable exactly when r_C(X₁,X₂)=0 for every X₁⊆X₂.

result_additive_variability_bound.reason: The stage lists, capacities, instability premises, and summed bound are all exposed.
result_additive_variability_bound.source_evidence: Pinned source 0d57324d02fc64c4c6b627c71c71cbbf93610b7f0b4b2138da1b436bb9234434; cited publication:535-540. A sequential composition of q-acceptant 1-unstable stages with variability bounds m_i has variability at most Σ_i m_i.
